pages.text: This is Azad. He is THREE. Sometimes FOUR. It depends on the day. But every single day — every single ONE — Azad is FAST. And FOCUSED. And STRONG.
MORNING! Grass still wet! The soccer ball wiggles up close. "Kick me, Azad," it says. "But — FOCUS." Azad squares his shoulders. Two eyes. One ball.
BOOT! WHOOSH! GOOOOOAL! The ball spins right into the net and cheers up at him: "STRONG! That's you!"
AFTERNOON! Ice cold! The puck slides in sideways. "Get me, Azad," it hums. "But — FOCUS." Azad tightens his grip on the stick. Two eyes. One puck.
WHISH! CLACK! GOOOOOAL! The puck skids into the corner of the net and cheers: "FOCUSED! That's you!"

SUNSET! The little red moto revs by the gate. "Ride me, Azad," it rumbles. "But — FOCUS." Azad grips the handlebars. Two eyes. One road. VROOM! VRRRRRROOOM! Down the path he zooms! The wind rushes past and cheers: "STRONG AND FOCUSED! That's you!"
Home. Cleats off. Skates off. Helmet on the hook. The moon peeks in through the window. "Big day," the moon says. "Big DAY," says Azad.

"One more thing to focus on, Azad. Your eyes... on my eyes." Deep breath in. Slow breath out. Eyes soft. Breath slow. And Azad — the FAST one, the FOCUSED one, the STRONG one — closes his eyes. And dreams the whole zoom-y day all over again.

vocab.kidDefinition: look at one thing so hard that nothing else can pull your eyes away
the small hard black circle that slides across the ice in a game of hockey
